findings.title: Invalid ERB closing statement prevents rendering existing discussions
findings.body: The opening conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. This produces invalid Ruby in the compiled template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. Change this to `<%- end %>` and exercise the endpoint with view rendering enabled.

findings.title: Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization and allow stored XSS
findings.body: Returning `raw` unchanged bypasses the rendering pipeline's HTML sanitization. The RSS poller passes external HTML directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, and `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts or event handlers. Consequently, feed content such as an image with an `onerror` handler is stored as executable cooked HTML under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to these posts also retain this bypass. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before storing or rendering their cooked content.

findings.title: Escape the source URL before interpolating it into HTML
findings.body: The source URL is inserted into both a single-quoted attribute and link text without escaping. A URL on the permitted host with a fragment such as `#'onclick='alert(1)` can pass URI host validation and fetch the original article, but produces an injected `onclick` attribute in the imported attribution link. This link is appended after Readability processes the article and is rendered through the raw-HTML path. Build the link with an escaping HTML helper rather than string interpolation.

findings.title: Handle RSS items that do not contain an Atom content field
findings.body: The poller unconditionally reads `i.content.scrub`, but valid RSS items commonly supply their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can have only a summary. For these feeds the content value is absent, causing the poll to fail before importing the item or any subsequent entries. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries without a body explicitly; add coverage using actual RSS and Atom fixtures.

findings.title: Resolve relative URLs without corrupting protocol-relative links
findings.body: Treating every leading slash as a root-relative path rewrites `//cdn.example.com/image.png` into a path on the article host, breaking protocol-relative images and links. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../other-page` remain unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the source article. Resolve both `href` and `src` against the full source URL with URI resolution instead of manually stripping slashes.

findings.title: Revalidate redirect destinations when retrieving an embedded article
findings.body: `TopicRetriever` checks only the host of the initial URL, while `open(url)` automatically follows redirects without applying that restriction. An allowed-host redirect to another host, including a loopback or private-network HTTP service, therefore makes the worker fetch an otherwise forbidden destination and potentially publish its response as a topic. Validate each redirect destination and reject private/internal addresses before making the request.

findings.title: Preserve the original thread creation date during Disqus imports
findings.body: The previous topic creation passed `t[:created_at]` to `PostCreator`; the replacement passes only the title, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` creates the first post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical timestamps, so imported topics now appear newly created and have replies dated before their opening post. Carry the original creation timestamp through the new import path.
